name: Matki Usal
subtitle: sprouted moth beans in a thin dark gravy of onion, roasted coconut and goda masala

ingredients.note: goda masala is the Maharashtrian original, if you can get it
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Sprouting matki takes two days: soak the beans 8 hours, drain, tie them in a damp cloth and leave in a warm place 24 to 36 hours until the tails are about 5mm.
Dry-roast the grated dried coconut until deep brown and grind it with the onion, garlic and ginger before you light the pan.
Rinse the sprouts and pick out any that have not opened.

steps.text: Grind the roasted dried coconut with half the onion, the garlic and the ginger to a coarse paste with 3 tbsp water.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing.
Add the remaining chopped onion and cook 6 minutes until golden at the edges.
Stir in the coconut paste and fry 5 minutes over medium heat until it darkens and stops smelling raw.
steps.tip: Keep scraping the base. Coconut paste catches fast.

steps.text: Add the chilli powder, kashmiri chilli, coriander powder, turmeric and garam masala and fry 1 minute.
Tip in the sprouts, turn them through the masala and cook 3 minutes.
Add the water, salt, jaggery and tamarind, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 18 minutes until the beans are soft but still hold their shape.
steps.tip: Pressure cooking is faster but turns them to mush. Eighteen minutes open is worth the time.

steps.text: Uncover and check the gravy: it should be thin, dark and slick with red oil on top. Loosen with hot water if it has tightened.
Finish with coriander and serve with bhakri, or with pav and chopped onion.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens as the beans drink the gravy; loosen with hot water when reheating. Freezes 1 month.
